paragraphs: Friend, here is what I want you to hold onto. The crowd shouts that Jesus is "the King of Israel!" (John 12:13), and then Jesus finds a young donkey and sits on it (John 12:14). He is the King, and He comes the way the written words said He would: "seated on the colt of a donkey." (John 12:15) What God says ahead of time, God does.

Now look at the disciples. "At first His disciples did not understand these things," but after Jesus was glorified they remembered and realized these very things had also been written about Him (John 12:16). That's good news for you and me, baker. If a piece doesn't land the first time, you're in good company, because the disciples were right there with the same problem.

One more thing, and it's the quiet one. The people who saw Lazarus raised "continued to testify," and the crowd came out because they heard about that sign (John 12:17-18). Then the Pharisees say, "Look how the whole world has gone after Him!" (John 12:19). So keep telling what you've seen of Him, friend, because those who testified were part of why the crowd went out to meet Him.
